terms.gloss: in my absence, while I am (was) away
terms.grammar: ablative absolute of absēns, absentis, participle of absum
terms.comment: Latin speaks of the absent person, not of an abstract absence: tē absente, in your absence; absentī mihi, to me while I was away.

evidence: Cic. Pis. 37: cōnfer absentiam tuam cum meā (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Classical but much rarer than the participle. Quintilian also uses it for the lack of something (absentia testimōniōrum, Quint. 5.7.1); for that sense see lack.

phrases.latin: complexus igitur sum cōgitātiōne tē absentem, epistulam vērō ōsculātus
phrases.english: so I embraced you in my thoughts in your absence, and kissed the letter

phrases.latin: ut certiōrēs facerēmus absentīs, sī quid esset quod eōs scīre aut nostrā aut ipsōrum interesset
phrases.english: to let those who are away know of anything that it matters to us or to them that they should know
What happened while I was away?

sources: Lewis & Short: absum · Lewis & Short: absentia
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 92, 267.
